question: Should OpenClaw add execute-on-parse tool execution to agent-core, and should it be a new opt-in `toolExecution` mode or a redesign of the existing `parallel` mode?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the fix changes core runtime ordering and security/product semantics rather than repairing an already-defined behavior contract.

options.title: Design an opt-in core mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for a new execute-on-parse path with transcript, hook, approval, cancellation, and ordering tests.

options.title: Backlog performance work
options.body: Leave the feature as a performance backlog item until maintainers decide the API and compatibility policy.

options.title: Reject early execution
options.body: Close or defer the request if maintainers want post-stream parallel execution to remain the only supported concurrency model.

recommendation.title: Design an opt-in core mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for a new execute-on-parse path with transcript, hook, approval, cancellation, and ordering tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central loop implementation and recent merged path history point to this owner as the best first reviewer for agent-core execution semantics.
